classes.name: accordion
classes.doc:
A bordered container for native <details>. The open state, the keyboard
and the accessible name are the element's. Deck restyles the summary,
replaces the marker with a chevron, and animates the height using
::details-content plus the interpolate-size opt-in in 02-reset.css — the
first time a disclosure could animate to auto height without JavaScript.
Give the details elements a shared name attribute for one-at-a-time.

classes.name: actions-cq
classes.doc: Button rows that go full width when cramped

classes.name: alert
classes.doc:
A block of prose the reader is meant to stop and read. The tone is a
three-pixel border-inline-start, so it moves to the right edge under
dir="rtl" with no second rule. Deck sets no ARIA role: role="alert" on
a message that is present at page load interrupts a screen reader
before it has read anything.

classes.name: alert-bad
classes.doc: Something failed, or is about to.

classes.name: alert-body
classes.doc:
The explanatory line. min-inline-size: 0 so a long unbroken string
cannot push the alert wider than its container.

classes.name: alert-good
classes.doc: Confirmation that something worked.

classes.name: alert-info
classes.doc: Something the reader should know before continuing.

classes.name: alert-title
classes.doc:
The first line of an alert. A weight change, not a heading — if it
belongs in the document outline, put this class on a real h2-h4.

classes.name: alert-warn
classes.doc: A consequence the reader should understand first.

classes.name: anchor
classes.doc:
Put .anchor on the trigger and --anchor on both trigger and panel.
Each pair needs a unique name, so generate it server-side in Keel:
<button class="anchor" style="--anchor:--menu-<?= $id ?>">

classes.name: app-shell
classes.doc:
Header, content, footer in a 100dvh grid whose middle row takes the
remaining height — the sticky footer, without the hacks. dvh rather
than vh so it tracks a phone browser hiding its chrome. It expects
exactly three children.

classes.name: avatar
classes.doc:
A round box holding an image or initials. --size drives the width, the
height and the font size together, so a size variant is one
declaration and the initials can never overflow the circle.

classes.name: avatar-lg
classes.doc: 56px.

classes.name: avatar-sm
classes.doc: 32px.

classes.name: avatar-square
classes.doc:
A square avatar, for anything that is not a person — an organisation,
a project, a repository.

classes.name: avatar-stack
classes.doc:
Overlapping avatars. The offset is a fraction of --size, so it stays
proportional at every size, and the ring is the surface colour, which
is wrong on any other background.

classes.name: avatar-xl
classes.doc: 80px.

classes.name: avatar-xs
classes.doc: 24px.

classes.name: back-to-top
classes.doc:
A link, not a button. #top is a real target at the head of the document,
so the browser moves focus there along with the scroll. A button calling
scrollTo() leaves a keyboard user parked at the bottom of the page while
looking at the top of it, which is the whole bug this component usually
ships with.
Showing and hiding is a scroll-driven animation, so there is no scroll
listener anywhere -- same mechanism as .scroll-progress in 16-motion.
visibility is in the keyframe on purpose: it takes the link out of the tab
order and out of the accessibility tree while it is off screen, which is
what aria-hidden reaches for and which CSS can actually do by itself.
deck.js only steps in where animation-timeline is missing, and it uses an
IntersectionObserver on a sentinel, not a scroll handler.

declarations.value: opacity var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out), visibility var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out), background-color var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out), scale var(--dur-2) var(--ease-spring)

classes.name: badge
classes.doc:
A small inline status pill. Sized in em, so it tracks whatever text it
sits next to rather than needing a size variant per context.

classes.name: badge-bad
classes.doc: Failed, overdue, rejected.

classes.name: badge-brand
classes.doc: Brand tint. For a label that names a category rather than a status.

classes.name: badge-dot
classes.doc:
Adds a leading dot in currentColor, so it takes the tone's text colour
without a second class. The dot is decoration — never ship one with no
text beside it, because colour alone is not a status.

classes.name: badge-good
classes.doc: Paid, shipped, passing, active.

classes.name: badge-solid
classes.doc:
Filled with the brand colour. The highest-emphasis badge; use one per
view or it stops meaning anything.

classes.name: badge-warn
classes.doc: Pending, expiring: needs attention, nothing is broken.

classes.name: banner
classes.doc: An announcement strip. Top or bottom, dismissible, out of the way.

classes.name: bar
classes.doc: Push the last child away from the rest

classes.name: btn
classes.doc: Every button clears the 44px touch target even when it looks smaller

declarations.value: background-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), box-shadow var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), translate var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: btn-3d
classes.doc:
A button with real thickness. The face moves down into the shadow instead
of just changing color.

declarations.value: 0 var(--lift) 0 0 color-mix(in oklab, var(--brand-600) 62%, var(--ink-900)), 0 calc(var(--lift) + 3px) 8px oklch(20% .03 var(--hue-neutral) / .22)

classes.name: btn-accent
classes.doc: A secondary emphasis colour, for upsells and highlights.

classes.name: btn-block
classes.doc: Full width. For a phone, or the primary action at the end of a form.

classes.name: btn-danger
classes.doc: Destructive and irreversible. Pair it with a confirmation.

classes.name: btn-ghost
classes.doc:
No border or background until hover. For toolbars and dense rows where
seven bordered buttons would be noise.

classes.name: btn-group
classes.doc:
Buttons joined into one control, with the inner radii and the doubled
border between them removed. Logical radii, so it mirrors under RTL.

classes.name: btn-icon
classes.doc: Square, icon-only button. It has no text, so it needs an aria-label.

classes.name: btn-lg
classes.doc: The large size, from --control-h-lg.

classes.name: btn-link
classes.doc:
Looks like a link, behaves like a button. Only for a real <button>
that has to sit in a row of links — on an anchor it adds a touch
target, a ring offset and nowrap to something that wanted none of them.

classes.name: btn-outline
classes.doc: Brand-coloured border, transparent fill.

classes.name: btn-primary
classes.doc:
The one important action in a view. Solid brand fill; use exactly one
per screen so it keeps meaning something.

classes.name: btn-round
classes.doc: A fully rounded button, usually paired with .btn-icon.

classes.name: btn-sm
classes.doc:
The 34px size. Still clears the 44px touch target, because the target
is a pseudo-element rather than the box.

classes.name: btn-soft
classes.doc: Tinted, low weight. Good for an action repeated down a list.

classes.name: bubble
classes.doc:
The message body. Its corner radii are logical, which is what lets the
grouping flatten the correct side in either writing direction.

classes.name: bubble-typing
classes.doc: Typing indicator

classes.name: card
classes.doc:
A surface with a border, radius and shadow. It brings no padding of its
own — put .card-body inside so the header, body and footer can each own
their spacing.

classes.name: card-body
classes.doc:
The padded region of a card. A column with a gap, so children stack
without margins.

classes.name: card-brand
classes.doc:
Brand-tinted fill and border, for the one card on a page that is an
offer rather than a record.

classes.name: card-flex
classes.doc: A card that turns into a horizontal media object once it has the room

classes.name: card-flush
classes.doc:
A card with no border, shadow or background. Grouping without a box
drawn around it.

classes.name: card-footer
classes.doc:
The top region of a card. A flex row, so a title and a control sit
on one line; the divider below it belongs to the header, so a card
with no header has no stray line.

classes.name: card-header
classes.doc:
The top region of a card. A flex row, so a title and a control sit
on one line; the divider below it belongs to the header, so a card
with no header has no stray line.

classes.name: card-link
classes.doc: Whole card is the link, but nested links still work

declarations.value: box-shadow var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: card-media
classes.doc:
An image region that reaches the card's edges. The card's own
overflow: clip does the rounding, so the image needs no radius.
Put it beside .card-body, never inside it.

classes.name: card-raised
classes.doc:
A deeper shadow and no visible border, for a surface that should read
as floating above the page.

classes.name: card-title
classes.doc:
The heading inside a card. Sized independently of h1-h6 so the same
card works at any heading level.

classes.name: carousel
classes.doc:
Scroll snap does the work. Arrows and dots are progressive enhancement,
so it still swipes correctly with JavaScript switched off.

classes.name: carousel-arrow
classes.doc:
Previous and next. Hidden on a coarse pointer, where the reader swipes
instead — so do not also hide the dots.

declarations.value: opacity var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out), scale var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: carousel-caption
classes.doc:
Text over a slide. The generous block-start padding is there to give the
scrim room to fade — without a background the near-white text sits
directly on the image and disappears over anything light.

classes.name: carousel-dot
classes.doc: the tap target is bigger than the dot

declarations.value: inline-size var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out), background-color var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: carousel-slide
classes.doc:
One slide. flex-basis: 100% by default; .carousel-peek makes it 86% so
the next one is partly visible, which is the only persistent cue that the
track scrolls once the scrollbar is hidden.

classes.name: carousel-track
classes.doc: The scroll-snap container holding the slides.

classes.name: center
classes.doc: Center a thing with a max width and no side effects

classes.name: chart
classes.doc:
The frame, and the palette. Six series colours are computed by rotating
--hue-brand, so charts retheme with the rest of the app and stay in one
family. That also makes them hard to tell apart for a colour-blind
reader — label the marks directly rather than relying on hue.

classes.name: chart-area-g
classes.doc: Area charts read better with a gradient falling off to nothing.

classes.name: chart-bar-fill
classes.doc:
The filled part of a horizontal bar, sized from --value. It grows from
the starting edge, which needs transform-origin — a physical property —
flipped for RTL in 19-logical.css.

classes.name: chart-bar-value
classes.doc:
The value printed beside a bar rather than inside it. Prefer this over
text on the fill: contrast-color() raises the floor for text on a series
colour but does not guarantee AA.

classes.name: chart-col
classes.doc:
A column. Its height is calc(var(--value) * 1%), so rendering a chart is
writing numbers into style attributes. data-label and data-value are drawn
as generated content, which means they are for sighted readers only.

classes.name: chart-col-stack
classes.doc: Stacked columns: nest segments inside a .chart-col-stack

classes.name: chart-columns
chart-group
classes.doc: Grouped columns

classes.name: chart-heat
classes.doc:
A grid of --cols columns whose cells mix the series colour with the
sunken background by --value, interpolated in oklab.

classes.name: chart-legend
classes.doc:
The key. Built from real buttons it gets a working toggle state for free,
because the faded style keys off [aria-pressed="false"].

classes.name: chart-svg
classes.doc:
<svg class="chart-svg" viewBox="0 0 300 100" preserveAspectRatio="none">
<path class="chart-area" d="..."/>
<path class="chart-line" d="..."/>

classes.name: chat
classes.doc:
Conversation view. Consecutive messages from one side group together and
only the last one in a run gets the tail.

classes.name: chat-composer
classes.doc: Composer pinned to the bottom

classes.name: chat-day
classes.doc:
A centred date pill between days. Styling, not structure — a screen
reader hears ordinary text.

classes.name: check
classes.doc:
A checkbox or radio and its text, laid out as a row that clears the
44px touch target. Wrap the text in .check-text to add a second line.

classes.name: check-card
classes.doc: Card-style choice, good for pricing and plan pickers

declarations.value: border-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), background-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out)
background-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: cluster
classes.doc: Horizontal group that wraps instead of overflowing on a phone

classes.name: cluster-between
classes.doc:
First item to one end, last to the other. Beware of combining it
with wrapping: each line is justified separately, so a lone item on
the second line jumps to the far end and looks stranded. .bar with
.push is the predictable version.

classes.name: cluster-center
classes.doc: Centres the row.

classes.name: cluster-end
classes.doc:
Packs the row against the end edge, which follows the writing
direction rather than always being the right.

classes.name: cluster-tight
classes.doc: Kept as the readable name for step 2, which is what most clusters want

classes.name: combo
classes.doc:
A filtering select. It wraps a real <select> that stays in the DOM and
stays in sync, so an ordinary form post works with no server-side
handling, server-side rendering is just marking options selected, and
without JavaScript the reader still gets a working control.

classes.name: combo-control
classes.doc:
The box, styled to match .input so a combobox in a form does not look
like a different species. Focus is handled twice — :has(.combo-input:focus)
and :focus-within — so a token's remove button lights the box too.

declarations.value: border-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), box-shadow var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: combo-create
classes.doc: Sticky "create new" row for tag-style inputs

classes.name: combo-empty
classes.doc:
The no-matches row. Name what was searched for — "No repositories match
'deckk'" tells a reader who mistyped what they actually typed.

classes.name: combo-group
classes.doc: A sticky heading above a group of options.

classes.name: combo-input
classes.doc:
The text field. deck.js gives it role="combobox" and keeps aria-expanded
in step; arrow keys move .is-active rather than focus, so the reader can
keep typing while the highlight moves.

classes.name: combo-list
classes.doc:
The option list. A positioned sibling by default, which a clipping
ancestor can cut off; 25-anchor.css moves it to the top layer where
anchor positioning exists, which is the fix for the combobox-inside-a-modal
bug.

classes.name: combo-loading
classes.doc:
The no-matches row. Name what was searched for — "No repositories match
'deckk'" tells a reader who mistyped what they actually typed.

classes.name: combo-option
classes.doc: The matched substring, wrapped by deck.js

classes.name: contain
classes.doc:
Tell the engine that a component's layout cannot affect anything outside
it. On a dashboard with twenty cards this is the difference between one
layout pass and twenty.

classes.name: container
classes.doc:
Centres content and caps it at --container, with the responsive page
gutter already applied. Nest one inside another and the inner one adds
a second gutter, so use .container-full instead.

classes.name: container-full
classes.doc:
Keeps the page gutter, drops the max width. This is what to nest
inside another container — a second .container would apply the
gutter twice.

classes.name: container-lg
classes.doc:
The same 76rem as the bare .container, named. Use it when a page
should say which width it means rather than rely on the default.

classes.name: container-md
classes.doc: An article with a rail, or a form.

classes.name: container-sm
classes.doc:
A single column of prose: about 70 characters at the body size,
which is inside the maximum line length WCAG recommends.

classes.name: container-xl
classes.doc: A wide dashboard or a data grid.

classes.name: copy
classes.doc:
The behaviour hangs off [data-deck-copy], not off .copy-btn. The class is
the look and nothing else, so a button with the class and no attribute
looks exactly right and does nothing at all -- the single most common way
to get this component wrong.
Whether a successful copy raises a toast depends on what is inside the
button: a .copy-done element swaps in place and no toast fires; without
one, deck-extras.js toasts instead. .copy-inline never toasts.

declarations.value: background-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: copy-inline
classes.doc: Inline icon-only variant, for an order number or an API key in a table

classes.name: coverflow
classes.doc:
A horizontal scroller where the off-center items rotate away. Uses scroll
snap for the mechanics and 3D only for the read.

classes.name: cq
classes.doc: Container queries: components respond to their slot, not the viewport

classes.name: cq-tone
classes.doc:
Query a custom property rather than a size. Set --tone on a container and
everything inside it adapts, with no extra classes on the children.
Supported in current Chrome and Safari; the fallback is simply no change.

classes.name: cube
classes.doc: Six faces for a rotating status block or an empty-state illustration.

classes.name: datefield
classes.doc:
The trigger for a date picker: an input with a calendar icon inside its
starting edge and a clear button at the end. The input is readonly and
cursor: pointer, because the value comes from the calendar — which also
means a reader who knows the date cannot type it.

classes.name: datepicker
classes.doc:
The calendar panel: a native popover, anchored to its field by
25-anchor.css with the same fallback chain as a menu. Where there is no
room below it opens upward, and position-try-order: most-block-size picks
the direction with the most room rather than the first that fits — which
matters more for a calendar than for a menu.

declarations.value: opacity var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out), translate var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out), overlay var(--dur-2) allow-discrete, display var(--dur-2) allow-discrete

classes.name: datepicker-day
classes.doc:
One day cell. 38px, raised to 42px on a coarse pointer so it approaches
the touch target. Eight is- states compose on it, and the range band is
built from is-in-range plus logical corner radii on the two ends.

declarations.value: background-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: datepicker-jump
classes.doc:
Opens the month and year grid. A picker without one makes a reader press
the next-month arrow twenty-four times to reach a date two years out.

declarations.value: background-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: datepicker-presets
classes.doc:
The shortcut rail — "Last 7 days", "This month". A horizontal scroller
below 40rem and a column beside the calendar above it.

classes.name: defer
classes.doc: Whole sections below the fold. Cheap and safe on any page.

classes.name: dg
classes.doc:
A real table with a frozen header and pinned columns. Use it when the
reader operates on data — sorts, selects, scans — rather than reads it;
.table is lighter for presentation. Must sit inside .dg-wrap, which
carries the scroll container and every custom property these rules read.

classes.name: dg-cards
classes.doc:
Below a breakpoint, restacks each row into a labelled card, taking the
column name from data-label on the cell. Costs the column alignment that
makes a grid comparable; prefer .dg-cq, which asks the container rather
than the viewport.

classes.name: dg-comfy
classes.doc: 56px rows, for a grid with two lines of content per cell.

classes.name: dg-compact
classes.doc: 34px rows and smaller text, for scanning many rows at once.

classes.name: dg-empty
classes.doc:
The row that holds an empty state, with its height and padding released
so the state can be any size.

classes.name: dg-resize
classes.doc: Column resize grip. deck.js writes the width to the th.

classes.name: dg-selection
classes.doc: Selection bar that slides in once rows are checked

classes.name: dg-sort
classes.doc:
The button deck.js builds inside a th[data-sort]. The styling keys off
th[aria-sort], so the arrow direction and the announced sort state are
the same value and cannot drift apart.

contextDeclarations.value: opacity var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), rotate var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: dg-virtual
classes.doc:
contain-intrinsic-size is the placeholder height for a skipped row. Get it
roughly right and the scrollbar is stable; the `auto` keyword makes the
browser remember the real height once a row has been rendered once.

classes.name: dg-wrap
classes.doc:
The shadow only appears once the grid is actually scrolled sideways.
A box-shadow offset is physical, so the geometry lives here and 19-logical
mirrors it for RTL once, rather than once per branch below.

classes.name: dg-zebra
classes.doc: Zebra is opt-in, and it never fights the pinned column background

classes.name: dir-ltr
classes.doc:
Sometimes a value has one true direction regardless of the page. An order
number, an account number, a URL, and a code block read left to right even
on an Arabic page. Isolate them so they do not scramble the text around
them.

classes.name: donut
classes.doc:
A conic gradient driven by --value, with .donut-center holding a figure
in the hole. One element, no SVG. Give it role="img" and a label — the
shape carries the meaning and nothing else conveys it.

declarations.value: radial-gradient(farthest-side, transparent calc(100% - var(--thickness)), #000 calc(100% - var(--thickness) + 1px))
radial-gradient(farthest-side, transparent calc(100% - var(--thickness)), #000 calc(100% - var(--thickness) + 1px))

classes.name: drawer
classes.doc:
A side panel. The bottom sheet is in 08-mobile; this one comes in from an
edge and is the right shape for filters, settings, and a mobile nav.

declarations.value: translate var(--dur-3) var(--ease-emphasized), display var(--dur-3) allow-discrete, overlay var(--dur-3) allow-discrete

classes.name: drawer-body
classes.doc:
The scrolling region. overscroll-behavior: contain stops a scroll that
reaches the end from chaining to the page behind.

classes.name: drawer-end
classes.doc:
Pins the drawer to the ending edge instead of the starting one. The inset
is logical and mirrors for free; the translate is not, which is why this
rule declares its own.

classes.name: drawer-footer
classes.doc:
The action row, pinned to the bottom. Pads for the home indicator with
max(--space-4, safe-area-inset-bottom).

classes.name: drawer-header
classes.doc: The title row. Pads for a notch with max(--space-4, safe-area-inset-top).

classes.name: drawer-title
classes.doc: The drawer's heading. Point aria-labelledby at it.

classes.name: drop-target
classes.doc: A list that is accepting a drop

classes.name: editor
classes.doc:
A toolbar over a contenteditable region. Deck styles the chrome; deck.js
wires the commands. The content area inherits .prose, so what you type
looks the way it will look when it is published.

classes.name: editor-content
classes.doc:
The editable region. Its placeholder comes from data-placeholder through
:empty::before, so it needs no element and no script to hide it.

classes.name: editor-count
classes.doc:
The character count. .is-over turns it red past data-limit — a soft
limit, since silently refusing keystrokes reads as a broken keyboard. The
server has to enforce it, and role="status" makes it audible.

declarations.value: background-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: editor-toolbar
classes.doc:
The tool row. Pressed state is [aria-pressed="true"], which deck-extras.js
rewrites from queryCommandState after every command and selection change,
so the toolbar reflects the caret rather than the last button pressed.

classes.name: emoji
classes.doc:
Pins the emoji font stack and metrics so an emoji renders at the same
size and baseline on Windows, iOS and Android instead of jumping
between them.

declarations.value: "Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji", "Noto Color Emoji", "Twemoji Mozilla", "Android Emoji", sans-serif

classes.name: emoji-grid
classes.doc: Emoji picker grid — drop your own set in

classes.name: emoji-tile
classes.doc: Emoji as an avatar or a status marker

classes.name: enter
classes.doc: One-shot, on load. Use for content that appears, not for every section.

classes.name: error
classes.doc:
A validation message below a control. Lightened for dark mode with
light-dark(), and aligned to flex-start so an icon stays on the first
line of a two-line message.

classes.name: expand
classes.doc:
Real height:auto transitions, no measuring in JS. Needs
interpolate-size, which tokens opts into on :root.

declarations.value: block-size var(--dur-3) var(--ease-out), opacity var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: fab
classes.doc: Floating action button, parked above the tab bar and the notch

declarations.value: scale var(--dur-2) var(--ease-spring), background-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: fade-swap
classes.doc: Anything that goes display:none can still animate out.

declarations.value: opacity var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out), display var(--dur-2) allow-discrete

classes.name: field
classes.doc:
One form control and everything attached to it: label, input, help
text, error. The vertical gap between them comes from here, so a field
never needs margins.

classes.name: field-row
classes.doc: Two fields side by side on anything wider than a phone

classes.name: field-row-cq
classes.doc:
Form fields that pair up inside their own container, not the viewport.
This is the one that keeps biting people: a two-up field row inside a
narrow modal should stay stacked even on a desktop.

classes.name: fieldset
classes.doc:
A bordered group of controls that answer one question. Its legend is
the group's accessible name, which is what a radio group needs and
what a .label above one does not provide.

classes.name: file
classes.doc:
A dashed drop zone wrapping a real file input. The input is 1px and
transparent rather than display: none, so it keeps its place in the
tab order, and :focus-within is what makes that focus visible. Deck
styles the zone; dropping needs a handler of your own.

declarations.value: border-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), background-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: flip
classes.doc:
Two faces, one footprint. Front and back are stacked in the same grid

classes.name: float
classes.doc:
Two things about the markup that this file cannot enforce and that fail
silently when they are wrong:

1. The label must come AFTER the control. Every lift selector below is
`~ label`, and the general sibling combinator only looks forward.
Label first and it simply never moves.
2. The control needs placeholder=" " (one space). Without a placeholder
attribute :placeholder-shown never matches, so the label sits lifted
over an empty field.

FINDINGS 61: .float.is-invalid only colours the label. .field.is-invalid
in 06-forms.css also reddens the control's border; there is no equivalent
rule here, so the same class name does two different amounts of work
depending on which wrapper it is on. :user-invalid is unaffected -- it
matches the control directly through the 06-forms.css rule.

classes.doc:
Three ways to say "something is happening", and the choice is only ever
about one thing: whether you know how much is left. .progress and .ring
do, .spinner does not. There is no standalone meter -- a bar drawn from a
value rather than from an element is .chart-meter, in 14-charts.css.

.progress goes on a real <progress>, so the element carries the value, the
maximum and the role. The two vendor pseudo-elements have to be written as
separate rules: a vendor pseudo-element in a shared selector invalidates
the whole rule for the other engine. Same constraint as .range.

Pushes this element and everything after it to the far end of a flex

classes.name: range
classes.doc:
A slider. The track and thumb are vendor pseudo-elements with
different names and different box models per engine, so every
declaration is written twice — WebKit needs a negative block-start
margin to centre the thumb and Firefox does not.

classes.name: range-pair
classes.doc:
Two stacked native range inputs. Real inputs mean real keyboard support
and a real form post; the track between them is drawn from --lo and --hi.

classes.name: range-readout
classes.doc:
The current value of a slider. Put it on an <output>, which is an
implicit live region, so the value is announced as the slider moves.

classes.name: range-ticks
classes.doc: Ticks under a single or paired range

classes.name: rating
classes.doc:
The inputs are written HIGHEST value first -- 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 -- and
row-reverse draws them 1 to 5. That is not a quirk, it is the whole
mechanism: to light a star and everything below it, the selector has to
reach forward from the chosen one, and CSS has no previous-sibling
combinator. Reversing the row turns "everything below" into "everything
after".

Get the order wrong and it fails recognisably: the stars fill from the
wrong end and the posted value is the mirror of the one clicked.

:focus-visible + label uses the ADJACENT sibling, so each label must come
immediately after its own input.

classes.name: rating-static
classes.doc: Read-only display: a fill percentage rather than whole stars

classes.name: ratio-16x9
classes.doc: Aspect boxes for media

classes.name: reaction
classes.doc: Reaction pill, like a Slack or Teams reaction

classes.name: ring
classes.doc:
A conic gradient for the fill, a radial mask for the hole. Three custom
properties shape it: --value, --size, --thickness.

The mask is the thing to understand. It applies to this element AND its
whole subtree, so a label centred inside a .ring is punched out along with
the middle -- it renders, it takes up space, it is in the accessibility
tree, and it is invisible. That is what .ring-wrap and .ring-label below
exist for: an unmasked wrapper that stacks the label over the ring as a
sibling rather than a child.

FINDINGS 60: place-items and the three font declarations here are the
fossil of the approach that does not work. They style a child nobody can
see -- .ring-label repeats all three on the sibling, which is the tell.
Due for removal; kept for now because the API is frozen.

classes.name: status-line
classes.doc: Live status line: dot plus label, the pattern used in status pages

classes.name: stepper
classes.doc:
A wizard. The timeline in 07 records what happened; this one shows where
you are in a process you are actively moving through.

classes.name: stepper-auto
classes.doc:
Horizontal where there is room, vertical below a breakpoint. Prefer this
over .stepper-vertical: four steps with notes do not fit across a phone,
and a horizontal stepper that squashes is unreadable.

classes.name: stepper-vertical
classes.doc: Vertical on a phone, where five steps side by side never fits

classes.name: sticky-top
classes.doc:
A sticky header. Where scroll-state container queries are supported
the blur and shadow live on an ::after that is transparent until the
header actually sticks, so in flow it looks like part of the page.
The treatment rides on a pseudo-element because a scroll-state
container can style its descendants but not itself.

classes.name: sweep
classes.doc: Underline that draws in from the start edge

classes.name: switch
classes.doc:
An on/off control that takes effect immediately, drawn over a real
checkbox. If the reader has to press Save afterwards, use .check
instead. Add role="switch" when "on"/"off" reads better than
"checked"/"unchecked".

classes.name: tab
classes.doc:
One trigger. Styled from [aria-selected="true"], so the visual state and
the accessible state are the same attribute and cannot disagree. The
unselected state carries the same transparent border, so selecting one
changes a colour and never moves anything.

declarations.value: color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: table
classes.doc:
A real table, kept a table at every width, because values in a column
are only comparable while the columns exist.

classes.name: table-compact
classes.doc: Tighter cell padding, for a table the reader scans rather than reads.

classes.name: table-stack
classes.doc:
Below 40rem, restacks each row into labelled lines, taking the label
from data-label on the cell. Every cell needs one. The thead is
clipped rather than removed, so header association survives; print
undoes the whole thing, because paper is never narrow.

classes.name: table-wrap
classes.doc:
The scroll container for a table, and not optional. It carries the
border, radius, background and overflow-x, without which a wide table
pushes the whole page sideways. Add tabindex="0" when the table
overflows, or a keyboard user cannot scroll it.

classes.name: tabs
classes.doc:
The strip. Scrolls sideways rather than wrapping, because tabs that wrap
stop reading as a strip. Deck styles the tabs and ships no keyboard
behaviour: if you use role="tablist" you must add the roving tabindex and
the arrow keys yourself, or the role promises what the page does not do.

classes.name: text-muted
classes.doc:
Secondary text colour. Still meets contrast against every surface Deck
defines, so it is safe for body copy rather than decoration only.

classes.name: text-sm
classes.doc: One step down the type scale, for secondary text and dense rows.

classes.name: textarea
classes.doc: Grows with its content instead of scrolling in a 4-row box

declarations.value: border-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), box-shadow var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), background-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: th-vertical
classes.doc: A rotated column header that still measures and aligns correctly

classes.name: tilt
classes.doc:
deck.js writes --tilt-x and --tilt-y from the pointer position. Both are
registered angles, so they interpolate smoothly back to rest.

declarations.value: rotate var(--dur-3) var(--ease-out), scale var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: tip
classes.doc:
The ::after tooltip could never flip. This one can, and it can carry a
real arrow that stays pointed at the anchor.

declarations.value: opacity var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out), overlay var(--dur-2) allow-discrete, display var(--dur-2) allow-discrete

classes.name: tip-arrow
classes.doc:
The arrow on a .tip. background: inherit takes the tip's colour, and
justify-self: anchor-center keeps it pointed at the trigger whichever way
the tip has flipped.

classes.name: toast
classes.doc:
One notification. The accent colour is a single custom property,
--toast-accent, which paints the edge, the icon and the timer together, so
a kind is one declaration. Built by Deck.toast() rather than written by
hand; touch-action: pan-y lets a horizontal swipe dismiss it while a
vertical drag still scrolls the page.

declarations.value: translate var(--dur-3) var(--ease-out), scale var(--dur-3) var(--ease-out), opacity var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out), margin var(--dur-3) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: toast-icon
classes.doc:
The leading glyph, coloured by --toast-accent so it matches the kind
without a rule of its own.

classes.name: toast-main
classes.doc:
The text column of a toast. min-inline-size: 0 so a long unbroken string
cannot push the close button off the end.

classes.name: toast-region
classes.doc:
The fixed container. pointer-events: none on the region and auto on each
toast, so the empty area does not swallow clicks on the page beneath. Sits
above a .tabbar when the page has one, and clears the home indicator.

classes.name: toast-timer
classes.doc:
The auto-dismiss bar. A CSS animation rather than a JavaScript countdown,
which is what allows hovering or focusing the region to pause every timer
in it with one declaration — so a reader moving toward an Undo button does
not have it vanish as they arrive.

classes.name: tooltip
classes.doc:
A CSS-only tooltip: the text comes from data-tip through ::after, so there
is no second element. It cannot flip near a window edge, cannot escape an
overflow:hidden ancestor, and is hidden entirely on a coarse pointer. Never
put anything essential in it, and pair it with aria-label — generated
content is not a reliable accessible name.

declarations.value: background-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), fill var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out), stroke var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out)
translate var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out), scale var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out), rotate var(--dur-2) var(--ease-out)
inline-size var(--dur-3) var(--ease-out), block-size var(--dur-3) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: video
classes.doc:
A responsive frame for a native video or an embed, plus styling for the
native controls where the browser allows it.

declarations.value: scale var(--dur-2) var(--ease-spring), background-color var(--dur-1) var(--ease-out)

classes.name: video-poster
classes.doc: Poster overlay with a play button, for a click-to-load embed

classes.name: virtual
classes.doc: Any long stack of cards: an activity feed, a chat log, search results

classes.name: vt-hold
classes.doc:
Elements that persist across the navigation. Give the same
view-transition-name to the matching element on both pages and the browser
tweens between them — a row in a list morphing into a detail header.

classes.name: with-indicator
classes.doc: A count or dot anchored to a corner of something

classes.name: writing-vertical
classes.doc:
Vertical text for a table header that would otherwise need a 40 character
column, or for a sidebar label.

classes.name: z-lift-1
classes.doc:
Lift an element toward the viewer inside a scene, rather than faking it
with a bigger shadow.
